description: A climbing aroid from Central American rainforests, grown for its large fenestrated leaves. Vigorous and forgiving, which makes it a common first 'statement' houseplant.
sapling_description: Plant a rooted cutting in chunky, free-draining aroid mix. Give it a moss pole early — fenestrations only appear once the plant can climb.

care.notes: Overwatering is the usual killer; let the top 5cm dry out first.

description: An upright succulent with stiff, banded leaves. Tolerates low light and long neglect, making it the most forgiving houseplant there is.
sapling_description: Root a leaf cutting in barely-damp sand. Expect two months before roots form — resist the urge to water more.

care.notes: Root rot from kindness is the only real risk; err on the dry side.

description: A trailing vine with heart-shaped leaves, often variegated. Grows in almost any light and roots in a glass of water.
sapling_description: Cut just below a node, sit it in water until roots reach 5cm, then pot into ordinary potting mix.

care.notes: Leggy growth with small leaves means it needs brighter light, not more water.

description: A shade-tolerant tropical with glossy leaves and white spathes. Wilts dramatically when thirsty and recovers within hours of watering.
sapling_description: Divide an established clump at repotting, keeping three or more leaves per division.

care.notes: Brown leaf tips usually mean tap-water fluoride — try filtered water.

description: A tender annual herb grown for its aromatic leaves. Fast-growing and productive, but intolerant of cold and drought.
sapling_description: Sow indoors after the last frost, thin to 20cm apart. Pinch the growing tip above the second leaf pair to force branching.

care.notes: Let it flower and leaf production stops — pinch buds off on sight.

description: A vigorous perennial herb that spreads by runners. Productive to the point of invasiveness in open ground.
sapling_description: Grow in a container, always — in a bed it will take over within two seasons.

care.notes: Never plant it in the ground unless you want only mint.

description: A heavy-cropping small-fruited tomato. Needs sun, consistent water and steady feeding once fruit sets.
sapling_description: Bury the seedling up to its first leaves — the buried stem grows extra roots. Stake at planting, not later.

care.notes: Irregular watering splits fruit and causes blossom-end rot.

description: A warm-season fruiting plant grown for pungent fruit. Slow to start, then productive for months.
sapling_description: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost; they need 25°C+ soil to germinate reliably.

care.notes: Stress the plant slightly with less water and the fruit gets hotter.

description: A stemless succulent with thick, gel-filled leaves used for burns. Needs bright light and very little water.
sapling_description: Separate an offset ('pup') with some roots attached, let the cut callus for two days, then pot in gritty mix.

care.notes: Mushy translucent leaves mean it has been watered far too often.

description: A tree-like succulent with thick glossy leaves. Extremely long-lived; specimens outlast their owners.
sapling_description: Break off a leaf, let it callus for three days, and lay it on dry soil. Roots follow in weeks.

care.notes: Leaf drop almost always means too much water, not too little.

description: An arching grassy plant that throws out plantlets on long stems. Nearly indestructible and safe around pets.
sapling_description: Pin a plantlet onto damp compost while still attached to the parent; cut it free once rooted.

care.notes: Brown tips are a fluoride reaction to tap water, not underwatering.

description: An upright tree with thick, glossy, burgundy-tinged leaves. Grows tall quickly in good light.
sapling_description: Air-layer a stem rather than taking a cutting — Ficus cuttings root slowly and unreliably.

care.notes: Hates being moved; sudden leaf drop usually follows a change of position.

description: A dramatic indoor tree with huge violin-shaped leaves. Rewarding but genuinely fussy about light and consistency.
sapling_description: Notch the trunk above a node to force branching; unpruned plants grow as a single bare stem.

care.notes: Brown crispy edges mean too little light; dark spreading spots mean too much water.

description: A woody Mediterranean sub-shrub with fragrant grey-green foliage and purple flower spikes.
sapling_description: Plant in gritty, alkaline, sharply drained soil. Never mulch with anything that holds moisture at the crown.

care.notes: Rich soil and heavy feeding produce soft growth and no scent.

description: An evergreen woody herb with needle-like aromatic leaves. Drought-tolerant once established.
sapling_description: Take a 10cm semi-ripe cutting in late summer, strip the lower leaves, and root in sandy compost.

care.notes: Wet feet in winter kills more rosemary than cold ever does.

description: A fast annual herb grown for its leaves and seeds. Bolts quickly in heat, so successive sowing is essential.
sapling_description: Sow directly where it is to grow — it resents transplanting and bolts if the roots are disturbed.

care.notes: Sow a fresh batch every three weeks; each plant is short-lived.

description: A small tropical tree whose aromatic leaves are essential in South Indian cooking. Frost-tender.
sapling_description: Grow from fresh seed — dried seed will not germinate. Keep the seedling above 18°C.

care.notes: Yellowing leaves usually mean it needs iron; feed with a micronutrient mix.

description: Holy basil — an aromatic perennial grown for tea, medicine and ritual use across South Asia.
sapling_description: Sow on the surface of warm, damp compost; the seed needs light to germinate.

care.notes: Pinch flower spikes to keep the leaves coming.

description: A bright annual flower widely used as a companion plant; its roots suppress soil nematodes.
sapling_description: Sow after frost, thin to 25cm. Deadhead weekly for continuous flowering.

care.notes: Too much nitrogen gives lush leaves and almost no flowers.

description: A tropical shrub with large, short-lived, brilliantly coloured flowers. Blooms continuously in warmth.
sapling_description: Root softwood cuttings in early summer with bottom heat.

care.notes: Bud drop means the plant dried out, even briefly.

description: A thorny climber grown for papery bracts in magenta, orange and white. Flowers hardest when slightly stressed.
sapling_description: Plant in a container barely larger than the root ball — restricted roots trigger flowering.

care.notes: Water and feed it generously and you get vigorous green growth with no colour.

description: A robust climbing aroid, widely grown across South Asia in water bottles and hanging pots.
sapling_description: A node cutting in plain water roots within two weeks; change the water weekly.

care.notes: Happy in water indefinitely, but will need liquid feed if never potted.

description: A clumping feather palm that brings height indoors. Thirsty and sensitive to dry air.
sapling_description: Buy as a clump; single seedlings take years to look like anything.

care.notes: Brown crispy fronds mean dry air — mist or group it with other plants.

description: A glossy, upright plant with underground rhizomes that store water. Survives conditions that kill everything else.
sapling_description: Divide the rhizomes when repotting; each piece with a growing point becomes a new plant.

care.notes: If you're unsure whether to water it, don't.

description: A classic arching fern for shaded, humid spots. Unforgiving of dry air and dry soil.
sapling_description: Divide the crown in spring, keeping plenty of roots with each piece.

care.notes: Dry air browns the fronds long before dry soil does.

description: An evergreen citrus that fruits in containers given enough sun and steady feeding.
sapling_description: Buy a grafted plant — seed-grown lemons take a decade to fruit and rarely come true.

care.notes: Yellow leaves with green veins mean it needs iron and magnesium.

description: A low perennial that fruits in its first summer and spreads by runners.
sapling_description: Plant with the crown exactly at soil level — buried crowns rot, exposed ones dry out.

care.notes: Mulch under the fruit to keep it off wet soil and away from slugs.

description: A compact plant with round coin-like leaves on slender stalks. Produces offsets generously.
sapling_description: Separate a pup once it has four leaves, cutting the underground runner cleanly.

care.notes: Rotate the pot weekly or it leans hard toward the light.

description: The common moth orchid. Epiphytic, so it grows on bark rather than soil, and flowers for months.
sapling_description: Pot in coarse bark only — ordinary compost suffocates the roots within a season.

care.notes: Soak and drain fully; an orchid sitting in water rots at the crown.

description: A small clustering cactus that flowers freely given a cold, completely dry winter rest.
sapling_description: Detach an offset, let it callus a week, then set it on dry gritty mix.

care.notes: No water at all from November to February — that dry rest is what triggers flowers.

description: An autumn-flowering perennial in a huge range of forms and colours.
sapling_description: Take basal cuttings in spring from the new shoots around the old crown.

care.notes: Pinch the tips twice before midsummer for a bushy, heavily flowered plant.

description: A fast cool-season leaf crop. Bolts as soon as the days get long and hot.
sapling_description: Sow direct in early spring or autumn, 2cm deep, thinning to 10cm.

care.notes: Grow it in spring and autumn only; summer sowings bolt before cropping.

description: A tall warm-season crop grown for its edible seed pods. Needs real heat to produce.
sapling_description: Soak the seed overnight and sow only once the soil is above 20°C.

care.notes: Pick pods at 8cm — a few days later they are woody and inedible.

description: Aubergine — a warm-season fruiting crop needing a long, hot season to ripen well.
sapling_description: Start indoors 10 weeks before planting out; seedlings stall badly if chilled.

care.notes: Stake early — a loaded plant topples and snaps at the base.

description: A braided-trunk tropical tree sold as a good-luck plant. Tolerates lower light than it looks like it should.
sapling_description: Sold pre-braided; keep the braid loose enough that the trunks can thicken.

care.notes: Yellow lower leaves mean it is being watered too often.

description: A trailing heart-leaf aroid, tolerant of low light and irregular care.
sapling_description: Node cuttings root readily in water or damp sphagnum.

care.notes: Very similar to pothos in care but prefers slightly more moisture.

description: A prayer plant with large silver-striped leaves that fold upward at night. Beautiful and demanding.
sapling_description: Divide at repotting, keeping each division well above 60% humidity while it recovers.

care.notes: Crispy edges mean dry air or hard tap water — use filtered or rainwater.

description: A clumping indoor palm with slim cane-like stems. Handles genuinely low light.
sapling_description: Grown from seed commercially; buy as an established clump.

care.notes: Check regularly for spider mites — dry indoor air invites them.

description: Arabian jasmine — an evergreen shrub with intensely fragrant white flowers that bloom through warm months.
sapling_description: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in summer under a plastic cover.

care.notes: Prune right after a flush of flowers; it blooms on new growth.

description: A tropical shrub with leathery leaves splashed in red, orange and yellow. Colour depends entirely on light.
sapling_description: Root tip cuttings with bottom heat; seal the cut end first, as the sap bleeds.

care.notes: Drops all its leaves after any sudden change — move it once and leave it alone.
